facts.fact_text: On 19 February 2008 a presidential election was held in Armenia.

Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the daily protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed at Freedom Square and the surrounding area around the clock, having set up a camp.
The applicant was an active participant in the rallies at Freedom Square, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins from 20 February 2008 onwards.
The applicant was present at Freedom Square when the police operation was conducted on 1 March 2008.
The applicant contested the Government's allegations and submitted that the assembly at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 had been peaceful and none of the demonstrators had been armed.
On 1 March 2008, apparently at some point between 6 and 7 a.m., police forces arrived on Freedom Square in Yerevan.
The applicant submitted that it was the police who had attacked the peaceful demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, using excessive force, in order to terminate the assembly.
As a result of the police operation on 1 March 2008, all the demonstrators present at Freedom Square, including the applicant, fled from the square.

According to the record of the applicant's bringing-in drafted by arresting police officers H.K. and E.K., the applicant was brought in to Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station from Freedom Square at 8.50 a.m. on 1 March 2008 on suspicion of having put up resistance to a police officer.

Police officer H.K. reported in writing to the chief of Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station that the applicant had been brought in from Freedom Square for having put up resistance by disobeying their lawful orders, refusing to be taken to the police station, pushing them and trying to flee.

Police officer E.K. reported in writing to the chief of Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station that the applicant had been brought in from Freedom Square for having put up resistance by disobeying their lawful orders, refusing to be taken to the police station, pushing them and trying to flee.
The applicant stated that he, H.M. and A.O. had been handcuffed and taken by car to Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station on 1 March 2008.

On 2 March 2008 the investigator drew up a record of the applicant's arrest, indicating that the applicant was suspected of having committed offences under Article 225.1 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (inciting disobedience to an order to terminate an unlawful assembly).

On 2 March 2008 the investigator drew up a record of the applicant's arrest, indicating that the applicant was suspected of having committed offences under Article 316 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (life or health-threatening assault on a public official).

On 4 March 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 225.1 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (inciting disobedience to an order to terminate an unlawful assembly) within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.

On 4 March 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (life or health-threatening assault on a public official) within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.
On 4 March 2008 the applicant was remanded in custody.

On 16 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).
On 16 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant to three years' imprisonment.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that Mr Ter-Petrosyan and a number of other opposition leaders and activists had organised and held unlawful demonstrations at Freedom Square.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that Mr Ter-Petrosyan and a number of other opposition leaders and activists had incited disobedience of the orders to end the unauthorised demonstrations.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that a number of demonstrators had illegally carried arms and ammunition and committed life- and health-threatening assault on police officers.

On 2 March 2008 the investigator drew up a record of the applicant's arrest, indicating that the applicant was suspected of having committed offences under Article 225.1 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (inciting disobedience to an order to terminate an unlawful assembly).

On 2 March 2008 the investigator drew up a record of the applicant's arrest, indicating that the applicant was suspected of having committed offences under Article 316 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (life or health-threatening assault on a public official).

On 4 March 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 225.1 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (inciting disobedience to an order to terminate an unlawful assembly) within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.

On 4 March 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 2 of the Armenian Criminal Code (life or health-threatening assault on a public official) within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.

The decision charging the applicant on 4 March 2008 stated that the applicant, having participated from 20 February 2008 in the unlawful assembly organised by Mr Ter-Petrosyan and his co-thinkers, incited disobedience of the orders to end the assembly, accompanied with public insults addressed at public officials.

The decision charging the applicant on 4 March 2008 stated that on 1 March 2008 at around 6 a.m., when police officers demanded participants in the demonstration at Freedom Square to allow verification of information that they possessed arms and ammunition and warned them to end the unlawful event, the applicant and other demonstrators disobeyed the police officers' lawful orders and committed life- and health-threatening assault on them, causing injuries of various nature and degree.

A summary of the relevant domestic law and practice, as well as of the relevant international materials, can be found in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia (application no. 23086/08, §§ 91-134, judgment of 20 September 2018).

The Government alleged that the purpose of the 1 March 2008 police operation at Freedom Square was the verification of information obtained by the police a day earlier, according to which the demonstrators possessed arms and ammunition.
The Government alleged that hundreds of demonstrators armed with metal rods and wooden clubs had gathered at Freedom Square, waiting for the police officers.
The Government alleged that the demonstrators attacked the police officers at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, hitting them and throwing stones, pointed metal objects and Molotov cocktails at them.
The Government alleged that numerous police officers were injured as a result of the demonstrators' attack at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that Mr Ter-Petrosyan and a number of other opposition leaders and activists had organised and held unlawful demonstrations at Freedom Square.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that Mr Ter-Petrosyan and a number of other opposition leaders and activists had incited disobedience of the orders to end the unauthorised demonstrations.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that a number of demonstrators had illegally carried arms and ammunition and committed life- and health-threatening assault on police officers.

The decision charging the applicant on 4 March 2008 stated that the applicant, having participated from 20 February 2008 in the unlawful assembly organised by Mr Ter-Petrosyan and his co-thinkers, incited disobedience of the orders to end the assembly, accompanied with public insults addressed at public officials.

The decision charging the applicant on 4 March 2008 stated that on 1 March 2008 at around 6 a.m., when police officers demanded participants in the demonstration at Freedom Square to allow verification of information that they possessed arms and ammunition and warned them to end the unlawful event, the applicant and other demonstrators disobeyed the police officers' lawful orders and committed life- and health-threatening assault on them, causing injuries of various nature and degree.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant had participated on a daily basis in mass public events, marches, around-the-clock demonstrations and sit-ins held continuously from 20 February 2008 in violation of the procedure prescribed by law and disrupting the capital's life, traffic, normal functioning of public institutions and peace and calm of the population.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that on 1 March 2008 at around 7 a.m., when police officers demanded the demonstrators gathered at Freedom Square to give them a possibility to verify the veracity of the information that the demonstrators possessed arms and ammunition and once again warned them to end the unlawful event, the applicant disobeyed the lawful orders of police officers H.K. and E.K. and assaulted them in a non-life or health-threatening way by pushing and pulling them.
The Government alleged that the members of the police force who arrived at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 were not equipped with any protective gear.
The applicant contested the Government's allegations and submitted that the assembly at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 had been peaceful and none of the demonstrators had been armed.
The applicant submitted that it was the police who had attacked the peaceful demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, using excessive force, in order to terminate the assembly.
The applicant stated that on 1 March 2008, early in the morning, police forces had arrived at Freedom Square and started violently dispersing the demonstrators gathered there.

The applicant stated that he had tried to persuade the police officers not to apply force at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, but had been attacked with tear gas and batons and had been pushed to the ground.
The applicant stated that after getting to his feet at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, he had walked towards Northern Avenue.
The applicant stated that two other demonstrators, H.M. and A.O., whom he knew personally, had walked along with him towards Northern Avenue on 1 March 2008.

The applicant stated that as he reached the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street on 1 March 2008, police officers had approached them, taken them by the arms and ordered them to follow to a nearby location.
Police officer H.K. stated that the demonstrators at Freedom Square, when ordered to terminate the assembly on 1 March 2008, had put up resistance, assaulted the police officers and fled.

Police officer H.K. stated that, having been given the task of pursuing and finding persons who had fled Freedom Square, he had stopped one man who was walking with a few others for an identity check at the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street on 1 March 2008.

Police officer H.K. stated that the man he stopped at the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street had been calm at first, but after being asked to follow him to a police station to check whether he had been involved in the unlawful events at Freedom Square, the man had pushed him and tried to flee.

Police officer H.K. stated that police officer E.K. had approached at that moment, and the man had pushed police officer E.K. as well, but then the man had surrendered to the officers and had been taken to Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station where he had been identified as the applicant.

Police officer H.K. stated that the two persons walking with the applicant had been taken away by other police officers before he had stopped the applicant at the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street.
Police officer E.K. made submissions similar to those of police officer H.K. regarding the events at the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street on 1 March 2008.
The applicant was questioned and denied having incited disobedience or inflicted any violence on the police officers.
On 27 March 2008 the applicant was questioned and once again denied having done anything illegal at Freedom Square.

On 27 March 2008 the applicant stated that when he had been approached in the street by the two police officers, he had been agitated because of the effect of the tear gas and had behaved in a way which was later assessed as unlawful.
On 27 March 2008 the applicant stated that he admitted his guilt for having assaulted the two police officers, H.K. and E.K., in a non-life and health-threatening way.
During the trial before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, the applicant retracted the admission of guilt he had made during the investigation and pleaded not guilty.

During the trial before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, the applicant stated that he had not assaulted the two police officers H.K. and E.K., who he alleged had made false statements.
Police officers H.K. and E.K. were questioned as witnesses before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan and maintained their statements against the applicant.

According to the applicant, he had been unable to question properly the police officers H.K. and E.K. in court as the trial judge disallowed some of the questions, namely those related to the lawfulness of the police actions at Freedom Square in the morning of 1 March 2008, as not related to the circumstances of the case under examination.

The applicant requested the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses, stating that they had been with him at the time of the alleged incident and had witnessed that he had not assaulted the two police officers H.K. and E.K.
In support of his request to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses, the applicant submitted written statements by H.M. and A.O. in which they corroborated his account of events.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan adjourned the examination of the applicant's request to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses until the other evidence in the case file had been examined.
On 15 May 2008 the applicant repeated his request to the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses.

On 15 May 2008 the applicant argued before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that the case against him, based solely on the statements of police officers H.K. and E.K., was trumped up and that he was basically prosecuted for having exercised his freedom of expression.

On 2 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan examined and dismissed the applicant's request to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses, holding that it was unnecessary to call them on the ground that there was sufficient evidence in the case file.
In reaching its findings, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan relied on the statements of police officers H.K. and E.K.

On 3 July 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal arguing that the trial court, by dismissing his request to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses and relying solely on the witness statements of police officers H.K. and E.K., had violated his right to a fair trial as protected by Article 6 of the Convention.
On 3 July 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal arguing that his prosecution and conviction had been in violation of Article 10 of the Convention.
On 3 July 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal arguing that his prosecution and conviction had been in violation of Article 11 of the Convention.
On 3 July 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal arguing that his prosecution and conviction had been in violation of Article 14 of the Convention.

During the examination of the applicant's appeal by the Criminal Court of Appeal, the applicant lodged a request to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses, similar to the one lodged before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan.
On 24 September 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld his conviction.

On 24 September 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's request to call H.M. and A.O. as witnesses, finding that the applicant's submissions were insufficient to conclude that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's dismissal of that request had been unfounded.

The Criminal Court of Appeal held that, as could be seen from the materials of the case, before police officers H.K. and E.K. had approached the applicant, both H.M. and A.O. had already been taken from the scene by other police officers and had therefore not witnessed the incident involving the applicant.
On 17 December 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law before the Court of Cassation, raising arguments similar to those raised in his earlier appeal.
On 22 January 2009 the Court of Cassation declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.
